To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rejection sensitivity is a dispositional tendency to expect, perceive, and react to rejection in a way that leads to hostile feelings and reactive aggression.

rejection sensitive people show increased hostility and aggression after perceiving rejection, which can elicit rejection from those who they value, and that this cycle can perpetuate rejection sensitive people’s social difficulties.
rejection sensitivity is a defensive motivational system that functions to protect the self from rejection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the processes by which rejection sensitive people become hostile and aggressive in response to rejection.
the role that rejection sensitivity plays in the rejection-hostility linkage and its role in the perpetuation of aggression in romantic relationships.
the ways that rejection sensitivity and hostile feelings are related to the experience of rejection, and how this experience is linked to aggression in romantic relationships.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
rejection sensitivity is a disposition to anxiously anticipate, readily perceive, intensely react to, and be motivated to avoid rejection.

rejection sensitivity is a defensive motivational system that is triggered by perceived social exclusion and elicits hostility and aggression in rejection sensitive people, which can perpetuate a rejection-hostility cycle.
the rejection sensitivity is a dispositional trait that can be defined as the disposition to anxieties expect, readily perceive and intensely react to social exclusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the experience of rejection can lead to hostility and aggression that can perpetuate rejection in close relationships.
rejection sensitivity functions in the service of protecting the self, but at the expense of the self and others.
rejection sensitive people have a difficult time regulating their hostile reactions to perceived rejection and this hostility can perpetuate the rejection they fear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rejection sensitivity is an important risk factor for aggression in close relationships.
rejection sensitivity, which is a stable trait, can be changed by learning new ways of responding to social threats.
rejection sensitive people are not necessarily aggressive, but they are more reactive to rejection and more likely to show hostility in response to rejection than less sensitive people.
